source: Has someone given you trouble? Made you uncomfortable in any way?
No, my lady. But Ophelia mentioned she saw me killed in a dream of hers.
Oh, Brit.
But it's more than that. That was merely an echoing of thoughts I've already been having.
I want to be near my family again. Near my mother and father. This castle is stifling.
Oh, Brit. Come now. Your father wants you here. With me.
I know you may not have settled into your role here yet, but to leave now would be dishonorable.
Your family worked hard, no doubt, to place you in my retinue. And my husband desires a better connection with the Brockenhuus family.
Your family worked hard, no doubt, to place you in my retinue. They wanted you at Elsinore for a reason. It's excellent exposure for a young lady.
Did you know your father and I have been discussing the possibility of a betrothal between you and Hamlet?
I did not, my lady. I would be-- er-- honored, of course.
We were even discussing the possibility of a betrothal between you and Hamlet. Things are different now, of course.
Listen, Brit. When I was but a girl I came to Elsinore and it felt to me, too, like a prison.
For years I thought I could never be happy here. Then, somehow, I found rapture. I found joy as a mother not only to my son, but to my country.
And what was once my prison became my domain. Soon it will be the same for you.
But you must be patient, my dear. Trust that your place here at Elsinore will bring great things.
Very well, my lady.
Thank you for the private audience.
I hoped you'd come.
I wasn't sure I would.
And yet, here I am.
And yet, here I am again.
What was it you wanted to discuss?
I... I wanted to apologize, first, I think. For coming upon you in your room, speaking nonsense.
I was beside myself. I didn't know where I was going. I was stumbling through the castle, and it was dark.
It had nothing to do with you, or with us. I was just lost.
I forgive you.
You do?
(Hamlet barging in is a constant I'll have to grow used to, at least for now.)
Of course. But now, I must admit, I find the notion of 'rekindling' our courtship rather a strange one.
After all, I've returned the letters you sent me and rebuffed your advances at every turn.
Yes. I know you've despised me from afar all summer. I wanted to respect that boundary.
Yet in a moment of desperation, you came running to find me?
I-it had nothing to do with you, or with us. Like I said, I was beside myself.
I'll say.
I swear, what is it about your power to cut me so? I can say nothing intelligent or curt in my own defense, even. I just let you tear right into me.
Does how I feel matter so little to you?
And when did you consider my feelings? You've been nothing but inconsiderate since we broke off our courtship!
I haven't properly apologized for how I treated you. Allow me to say this: I am sorry. Deeply and truly. I was wrong.
And if there's even the faintest chance... you told me you loved me, once.
So I did.
But no longer? If your heart has truly changed, I'll go, and I'll never trouble you again with my affections, nor stumble blindly into your room at dawn.
You have only to say the word.
Does it matter? I am powerless to choose to love you, even if I could.
What does that mean?
You know well. The forces at work in Elsinore are far stronger than whatever I might desire.
Your uncle looks at me as what I am: an obstacle to you becoming betrothed to someone else. Haven't you noticed?
I have never had any intention of allowing my uncle to run my life.
Everyone in this castle looks at me as what I am: an obstacle to you becoming betrothed to someone else. Haven't you noticed?
I have never had any intention of allowing others to run my life.
Listen. I am Prince of this country. And someday, God willing, I will be King. What could you desire that would be beyond my power to control?
It is because you are Prince that you cannot possibly understand.
You and I are bound by different privileges. That's a truth of this castle.
And what if it weren't?
No. You've been right to stay away from me.
The more I think on it, the heavier my heart becomes. I--
Ophelia, I know there's a world where you and I can be free. I believe in that world with all my soul.
But first, I need to strengthen myself for vengeance against my uncle.
And until that comes to pass, I can think of little else.
Just—I beg you—know that my belief in that future is the thing driving me to this vengeance.
Once my dark work is complete, I'm going to return for you, and I'm going to show you that things can be different.
You'll see.
(I see. While his uncle's crime still stands unanswered, he's focused solely on revenge.)
(But soon he's going to act against Claudius. And then—)
(Then perhaps he'll find me.)
(I wonder what the outcome would be if circumstances were different.)
Your 'dark work'? What do you mean by that?
Think nothing of it. Go. Fret on lighter things.
That was cruel.
Not meeting me. Written me off entirely, have you?
I waited by the pond. I am a fool after all, I suppose.
You won't make a fool of me again.
Mother! Uncle. To what do I owe this pleasure?
Your mother and I demand an audience with you. Since you have not sought us out, we come to find you.
Love, not so prickly. Calm yourself, please.
Ergh. What I intended to say was: We'd like to speak to you about reconciliation.
Lady Ophelia observed you've been menacing towards her.
Always a keen eye, that one. Nothing escapes her observation.
This period of mourning has gone on far too long.
The young earth lies lazily-packed on my father's ribs, and you're ready to settle into his throne. That's how it is, isn't it?
I am your uncle by blood and father by law. I order you to listen to me without retort.
You've no place intimidating the people of this castle. Women especially. It's crude, and beneath a young lord of your standing.
Men must be strong, stalwart, and noble in this house. To perform otherwise shames the Danish crown.
And furthermore—
I'm leaving.
Darling, no, please stay!
I think this 'intervention' has run its course.
My love, you must be tender with him.
Why? Because the sniveling brat can't handle the touch of a firm hand? My brother was a fool of a father, and the boy is weak as a result.
Some noble hearts cannot be beaten into obedience. But love them well, and they will love back, ever faithful.
My son is such a heart.
Enough. It was a waste to come here. For all of us.
You actually came.
When a beautiful woman beneath my station calls, who am I to resist?
You do have a history with that, don't you.
Why don't you come a little closer? It's terribly dark.
Mm. Much.
I wanted a moment to speak with you. I've heard some rumors about you and me lately.
I know my father called upon the Queen to approach the subject of a betrothal.
Yes. Do you think there's still any truth to it? Or was your mother merely gossiping?
I'm sure it's real. Discussions of whom I ought to marry are as old as I am. Older still, perhaps.
But I pay no mind to those sorts of matters until I must answer to them.
You know, it was cruel of you to have Ophelia ask me to meet you tonight.
It might have given her the wrong impression. I'd hate to hurt her.
Oh, hmph. As if I care what that hysterical hanger-on thinks.
What did you call her?
S-She's strange! It's not just me! Everyone thinks so! H-how could you--
Ophelia is a Lady of Denmark. The same as you. And from the look of it, she's three times the woman you are.
Don't you ever treat her cruelly again.
Stop. You're—scaring—me—
You evil girl. You don't think I see how manipulative you are? Just how stupid do you think I am?
Ow... My god, you really are insane, aren't you? I'm leaving. How dare you push me!
She's right.
I am insane. Or swiftly becoming so.
Hahaha... ha... haha!
Hamlet. You actually came.
My darling son! Lady Brit! What a pleasure!
Your Majesty!
I do so love strolling out in the utter darkness at midnight, alone. Don't you?
Especially unchaperoned!
We were merely talking, my lady.
Oh? What about?
Idle things.
T-The moon is quite full.
Oh, of course! I have often known you to take an interest in the phases of the moon, Hamlet.
Well, I hope you won't mind if I take my leave of you two, children. I grow tired.
And Brit, I believe you've some needlepoint to attend to, haven't you?
Ugh. There's always needlepoint to attend to.
I ought to go.
And I as well.
I should update Irma on the card game. I'm sure she'll be pleased.
You say they'll be there for the game?
That's what they told me.
Most excellent. Time to break out the old liar's deck!
Irma never plays a fair game of cards!
Wait. What about the key to Gertrude's room?
It's true. A deal is a deal.
Truth be told, I never keep that old thing on me. I stash it in the shrubberies by Gerta's room.
You can go fetch it yourself. I have cards to play!
I should report back to Brit.
You did it? Thanks. I'm sure he and I will have a wonderful evening.
And it's all thanks to you, 'Feely.
But you know, I'll be keeping my key all to myself.
But you promised!
Oh, don't go getting your undergarments rustled. There's another way in.
Irma stores her key in the plants outside Gertrude's chambers. I don't think she realizes I know.
If it happened to go missing for a while, who would notice?
Hello, Irma.
Ah, Gerta. Come to bother this old woman?
Don't be like that. I'm sorry I haven't been by recently. I've been busy.
Yes. I've been cooking. You've been ruling. Everyone's busy.
Well, I'm here now!
How is that fat husband of yours?
You shouldn't speak of him like that.
I suppose he's grown rather round in the past months, hasn't he?
It was not an insult. Fat is happy! Fat is proud!
He eats everything I make! He keeps me busy. His appetite is a compliment.
You know, Norway has extended an olive branch. I'm hoping that will help put Claudius at ease.
A peace offering from the Prince of Norway? You think it is genuine?
There is the possibility Norway will betray us, you know. It's possible the peace agreement wasn't genuine.
